name: device-code-entry
title: Device code entry
description: The page behind a CLI or TV login: type the short code from the device, check which device it is, then approve or deny.
docs: onSubmitCode(code) receives the code as the device shows it, in groups (WDJB-MJHT), and returns { deviceName, location?, requestedAt? } to move on, or a string for a code that is wrong or expired, which is announced and leaves the code in the boxes for correcting; a throw shows a general message. The boxes take only the characters of alphabet (default twenty consonants, so O and 0 can never be confused; cleanDeviceCode and formatDeviceCode are exported from device-code-entry/code): letters are upper-cased as typed, a character outside the alphabet is stopped before it lands and named in a polite line, and pasting works in any case, with or without the hyphen. codeLength (default 8) and groupAfter (default 4) shape the boxes. Step two asks Connect {client} on {device}? (clientName and account are yours) with the device, its approximate location, when it asked (written with locale and timeZone, with the zone's name after the time) and the code as facts, the line Only continue if you started this on your own device, and Approve and Deny as two buttons of one size; onApprove and onDeny may return promises, and the answer is shown and announced. defaultCode, defaultError, defaultRequest and defaultOutcome set the start for previews; locale, timeZone, footer, titleAs and labels work as in the other auth cards.
